quests.instruction: You walk quickly down the street. Which body parts swing back and forth beside you, opposite to your legs?
quests.hint: They help you keep your balance as you step.
quests.explanation: When your right leg steps forward, your left arm swings forward too. This swing helps keep you steady.
quests.funFact: Swinging your arms while you walk helps you save energy.

quests.instruction: You hike along a bumpy trail with rocks and roots. Which joints tilt your feet from side to side so you stay upright?
quests.hint: They sit just above your feet.
quests.explanation: Ankles tilt your feet to fit uneven ground, so your body can stay balanced.
quests.funFact: Your ankles make tiny adjustments many times a second without you noticing.

quests.instruction: While you walk, your body bounces up and down a little, but your head stays quite steady. Which part helps most to keep it that way?
quests.hint: It connects your head to the rest of your body.
quests.explanation: Neck muscles quietly soak up the bounce of each step, so your head and eyes stay steady.
quests.funFact: A steady head keeps the picture from shaking, so you can see clearly while you move.

quests.instruction: You crouch low and spring up into the air. Which body parts push you off the ground?
quests.hint: They are your longest and strongest limbs.
quests.explanation: Jumping starts with your legs, which straighten fast to launch you upward.
quests.funFact: Swinging your arms upward as you jump helps you go higher.

quests.instruction: You land after a jump. Which joints should bend a little to soak up the landing?
quests.hint: Landing with them locked straight can hurt.
quests.explanation: Bending your knees spreads out the force of landing, which is gentler on your body.
quests.funFact: Dancers call a soft knee bend before and after a jump a plié.

quests.instruction: Sprinters have big muscles at the top of their legs to drive each stride. Which part is that?
quests.hint: It is between the hip and the knee.
quests.explanation: Thigh muscles are some of the largest in the body, and they power sprinting, jumping, and climbing.
quests.funFact: In a sprint, each foot spends less than a tenth of a second on the ground.

quests.instruction: You balance on one foot. Which parts of that foot grip the floor to help you stay steady?
quests.hint: They help your foot grip the floor.
quests.explanation: Toes spread and press into the floor, and tiny muscle adjustments help you stay upright.
quests.funFact: Practicing balance makes the small muscles in your feet and ankles stronger.

quests.instruction: Dancers pick a spot on the wall and keep looking at it while they spin. Which body parts do they keep fixed on the spot?
quests.hint: They help you see where you are.
quests.explanation: Looking at one fixed point helps your brain keep track of where you are, so you feel less dizzy.
quests.funFact: Dancers snap their heads around to find the spot again on every turn, which is called spotting.

quests.instruction: You sit on a wobbly exercise ball. Which muscles at the front of your middle tighten to keep you upright?
quests.hint: They wrap around the front of your middle like a belt.
quests.explanation: The muscles around your tummy and back work together to keep your body steady.
quests.funFact: Together, these middle muscles are called your core.

quests.instruction: You color a small picture without moving your whole arm. Which joint lets your hand make small circles?
quests.hint: It is between your hand and your forearm.
quests.explanation: The wrist lets your hand move in small circles and short strokes while your arm stays still.
quests.funFact: Many artists draw big shapes with the whole arm and fine details with just the wrist and fingers.

quests.instruction: At a desk, you lean on your folded arms. Which pointy part of your arms rests on the desk?
quests.hint: They point out when you fold your arms.
quests.explanation: When you lean on a desk, your elbows carry the weight of your upper body.
quests.funFact: Leaning hard on your elbows for a long time can make your hand tingle, because a nerve there gets pressed.

quests.instruction: You hold your phone in one hand and tap the screen. Which part of that hand does the tapping?
quests.hint: It swings across your palm easily.
quests.explanation: Your thumb can swing across your palm, so it can tap every corner of a phone while your other fingers hold it.
quests.funFact: The joint at the base of your thumb is shaped like a saddle, which lets it move in many directions.

quests.instruction: In an overhand throw, which joint snaps straight at the end, like cracking a whip?
quests.hint: It unfolds in the last moment of the throw.
quests.explanation: The elbow unfolds fast at the end of a throw, adding speed to the ball.
quests.funFact: Top baseball pitchers can throw faster than 150 kilometers per hour.

quests.instruction: In a basketball chest pass, you start with the ball held against which part of your body?
quests.hint: Your ribs are right behind it.
quests.explanation: You push the ball straight out from your chest to a teammate, which keeps the pass quick and low.
quests.funFact: The chest pass is one of the first passes new players learn, because it is fast and easy to aim.

quests.instruction: To throw a flying disc, you flick it with a quick snap of which joint?
quests.hint: It bends your hand toward your arm.
quests.explanation: A flick of the wrist gives the disc spin, and the spin keeps it flying straight and steady.
quests.funFact: A spinning object holds its direction better, which is why footballs and bullets spin, too.

quests.instruction: In soccer, you pass the ball along the ground with the inside of which body part?
quests.hint: You wear cleats on them.
quests.explanation: The inside of the foot is wide and flat, so passes made with it are accurate.
quests.funFact: Pro soccer players can run around 10 kilometers during one match.

quests.instruction: To keep a hula hoop spinning, you swivel which narrow part of your body in circles?
quests.hint: A hoop spins around it.
quests.explanation: Moving your waist in circles pushes the hoop along, so it keeps spinning.
quests.funFact: A heavier hoop is easier to keep spinning than a very light one, because it turns more slowly.

quests.instruction: Before a forward roll, you tuck which part toward your chest so you roll over your back and not your head?
quests.hint: It points down when you nod.
quests.explanation: Tucking your chin keeps your neck safe and lets you roll over the curve of your back.
quests.funFact: Rolling on a soft mat spreads the force of the roll across your back.

quests.instruction: You bow politely, keeping your legs straight. Which joints do you bend?
quests.hint: You bend them to fold your body forward.
quests.explanation: In a bow, you bend forward from the hips while your knees stay mostly straight.
quests.funFact: People bow as a greeting in many countries, such as Japan and Korea.

quests.instruction: You arch like a cat to stretch. Which part of your body curves up like a hill?
quests.hint: It is the long part behind you, between your neck and your waist.
quests.explanation: Rounding and arching your back gently stretches your spine and the muscles along it.
quests.funFact: Gentle stretching after exercise helps muscles feel loose.

quests.instruction: To bend your elbow, which body parts pull on your bones like ropes?
quests.hint: They get shorter when they tighten.
quests.explanation: Muscles tighten and get shorter, which pulls on the bones and bends the joint.
quests.funFact: Muscles can only pull, never push, so they work in pairs: one to bend a joint and another to straighten it.

quests.instruction: Which hard parts inside your body give you shape and give muscles something to pull on?
quests.hint: Together they make up your skeleton.
quests.explanation: Bones support your body, protect the soft parts inside, and work with muscles to move you.
quests.funFact: Babies are born with about 300 bones, and some join together as they grow, leaving about 206 in adults.

quests.instruction: Strong, tough cords join your muscles to your bones. What are they called?
quests.hint: Think of ropes tying muscle to bone.
quests.explanation: Tendons pass the pull of a muscle on to a bone, so the bone moves.
quests.funFact: Tendons are tough like thick rope and do not stretch much.

quests.instruction: Which muscle in your chest never takes a break, beating day and night?
quests.hint: You can feel it thump after running.
quests.explanation: The heart is a muscle that squeezes again and again, pushing blood around your body.
quests.funFact: A heart beats about 100,000 times in a day.

quests.instruction: You ride a bicycle. Which body parts press down on the pedals?
quests.hint: They rest on the pedals the whole ride.
quests.explanation: Your feet press the pedals around in circles, powered by your leg muscles.
quests.funFact: A bicycle lets you travel much farther on the same energy than walking does.

quests.instruction: When you ride, which parts of your hands squeeze the brake levers?
quests.hint: They wrap around the handlebar.
quests.explanation: Fingers squeeze the levers to slow the bike, so keep them ready near the brakes.
quests.funFact: Using both brakes together helps you stop smoothly.

quests.instruction: Music plays, and you tap your foot in perfect time. Which parts pick up the beat?
quests.hint: They are how the music reaches you.
quests.explanation: Your ears pick up the beat, and your brain turns it into movement, so your foot taps in time.
quests.funFact: Even babies move to a steady beat.

quests.instruction: In a good throw, movement flows from the middle of your body out to your fingertips. Which of these moves last?
quests.hint: It is the joint closest to your hand.
quests.explanation: The twist begins in the waist, moves through the shoulder, and ends with a flick of the wrist.
quests.funFact: This chain of movement makes a throw much faster than moving the arm alone.

quests.instruction: Which joint bends like a door hinge, mostly forward and back?
quests.hint: It is the joint you bend to pull your hand toward your shoulder.
quests.explanation: The elbow works like a hinge. The shoulder and hip can swing in circles instead.
quests.funFact: The joints in your fingers and knees also bend mainly in one direction, like hinges.

quests.instruction: An ice skater spins slowly with arms stretched wide, then pulls them in tight. Which parts move in?
quests.hint: They stretch out from your shoulders.
quests.explanation: Pulling the arms in close makes the spin speed up, which is why skaters do it.
quests.funFact: Fast spinning skaters can turn several times every second.
